_comment: Assay definition for amphid.
This file holds what makes an assay a particular assay: the control tag,
the library construct, the index primer set, and the tolerances tuned
around them. Swapping it is how the pipeline is pointed at a different
panel or a different construct, without touching code.
What is deliberately NOT here: the sample_type and seq_type vocabularies,
and the structure of assignment. The logic depends on those - neg_extraction
sets thresholds, mock carries an expected composition, control requires a
parent - so making them configurable would mean every downstream branch has
to handle categories it knows nothing about. Configurability is not free.
The reference panel is data, not configuration, and stays a separate input.
Both preflight.py and Nextflow read this file, so the values are defined
once rather than duplicated between a config and a script.
name and version are recorded in preflight_summary.json, so a result can
always be traced back to the assay definition that produced it.
name: ampseq_helminth
description: Helminth ITS2/cox1 amplicon panel, two-step Nextera PCR, tandem-duplicated dual indices, plasmid decoys and spiked quantification standards

_comment: Inserted into each control plasmid and absent from every target, so
target-versus-control is a deterministic presence test rather than an
alignment-score comparison.
max_edits is generous on purpose. An 18bp tag matched exactly loses
about 30% of control reads at nanopore error rates, and every control
read called as target is a false positive in a real sample - the worst
error this assay can make. There is only one tag, so nothing competes
with it and generosity costs nothing. This is the opposite of the
barcode case, where the set's own minimum edit distance caps tolerance.
Edit distance rather than Hamming: the tag contains TTT, and homopolymer
indels are nanopore's signature error.
anchored means the search tests one window at the expected position
rather than scanning the read. At 3 edits a window matches by chance
about once in 2.9M, so scanning a 500bp read would give thousands of
spurious control calls per run instead of single digits.
Err toward calling a read control. A control read called as target
is a false positive; a target read called as control costs only a
little sensitivity.
Two-step PCR. PCR1 adds the Nextera overhangs to locus-specific primers;
PCR2 adds P5/P7 tails and the tandem-duplicated indices.
After orientation normalisation to the i5-forward strand, both indices
read in the same orientation as the index list: the i5 primer carries
the index forward, and the i7 primer carries its reverse complement,
which the top strand reverses back.
The 19bp mosaic end AGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG is shared by both overhangs, so
it cannot identify which end of a molecule is being read. The anchors
to use are the discriminating portions abutting each index window.
barcode_repeats 2 is the AMPSEQ tandem design; 1 is a conventional
single index at each end. Both are dual-index. The difference is that
the duplication is indel insurance: an indel makes one copy
uninformative and the other carries the read, and a frame slip yields
two copies that disagree, which is what detects it. With one copy
there is no second observation.
allow_indels is false regardless, because the i7 set's minimum edit
distance is only 2 - it tolerates one substitution but zero indels.
The index map encodes plate position: i5 gives the row (A-P), i7 the
column (1-24). So well is derived, never recorded.
Quants are spiked post-extraction at a fixed amount per fixed amount of
faecal DNA, so the unit is copies per unit DNA, not copies per gram of
stool. Two standards two orders of magnitude apart give a bracket, not
a curve: estimates inside are interpolated, outside are flagged as
extrapolated rather than reported with false precision.
A post-extraction spike normalises everything downstream of extraction
and nothing upstream, and the failure mode is directional - poor
extraction presents as low burden rather than as assay failure.
Tuning rather than identity. Tightening these makes pre-flight fussier;
loosening lets more through.
Nominal per-base error rates, used to forecast tag detection in the
pre-flight report so a decoy that is reliable on Illumina but marginal
under a fast basecalling model is known in advance rather than
discovered in the data.
